test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 04 Feb, 2026 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1. Soon all was quiet in the house: everyone was asleep.
A. The snowstorm had not subsided; the wind blew in their faces as if trying to stop the young criminal.
B. Her maid followed her with two bundles.
C. They descended into the garden.
D. Masha wrapped herself in a shawl, put on a warm cloak, took her small box in her hand, and went down the back staircase.
S2. With difficulty they reached the end of the garden.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentences need to be rearranged logically to maintain the coherence and unity of the paragraph.
 
• **Sentence D** introduces the action of Masha preparing to go out and descending the stairs, so it is the first logical sentence after S1.
 
• **Sentence B** follows as it describes her maid accompanying her with bundles, which logically connects to Masha preparing to leave.
 
• **Sentence C** comes next as it describes their descent into the garden, continuing the sequence of events logically.
 
• **Sentence A** is placed last before S2 as it describes the challenging weather conditions they faced after reaching the garden, leading to the final sentence.
 
• The correct sequence is **DBCA**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Understanding the structure:** Rearranging the sentences logically involves identifying the flow of events and connections between sentences.
 
• **Key points for coherence:**
 
 
• Identify the introductory sentence that sets the scene or introduces the main action.
 
• Ensure sentences follow a logical chronological order or thematic connection.
 
• The concluding sentence should wrap up the paragraph cohesively.
 
 

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

"Soon all was quiet in the house: everyone was asleep. Masha wrapped herself in a shawl, put on a warm cloak, took her small box in her hand, and went down the back staircase. Her maid followed her with two bundles. They descended into the garden. The snowstorm had not subsided; the wind blew in their faces as if trying to stop the young criminal. With difficulty they reached the end of the garden."</div
